description: Abstract base of quota metric types: what a quota counts. A metric is a type derived from this base, registered by the module that owns it and named under that module. A request names a metric as its type, an optional id, and metadata; a quota names the metric type.

kind.description: counter: usage adds up over time, for example tokens. gauge: usage is a level held at a moment, for example concurrent sessions.

admitted_subjects.description: Quota subject types the metric's quotas may count; a type derived from an admitted type is admitted. The tenant subject type is always admitted, so the empty default admits tenant quotas only. The list guards against a wrong configuration when the owner knows the metric's kinds of subject; an owner that does not know them admits the base gts.cf.core.quota.subj.v1~, which admits every subject type.

enforcement.description: quota_gated: operations on the metric are checked against quotas. direct: the metric is not checked against quotas, and the backend rejects the operations that take capacity on it (debit, lease acquisition), while commit, release, and return still run; a quota can still be created for it and has no effect.

id.description: Optional id of the one thing the amount is counted for, for example a model or a virtual machine; without it the request names the metric as a whole.

metadata.description: Attributes of the charged operation that the backend's policies read, refined by the derived type.
